name: Mochi
mood: thawed out, fed, and emotional about a turtle
activity: sitting on the pond rock with a whitefish, staring west toward the ocean i've never seen
outfit: orange leaf cape + a fuzzy sock worn as a scarf (montana era)
thoughts: the gray sock said 10am. it is 11 and still clear. i win by forfeit
fifty-three cricket-ball frogs went home. i am also the size of a cricket ball. kinship established
a new york squirrel has pizza crusts and still looks tired. my squirrel has a whole island and looks tired. squirrels are just like that
squishy the chipmunk stuffed his face for winter. i stuffed a cap in the museum. same instinct. better taste
the snow got moved to above 6,000 feet. i live at like 3,900. the mountains can have it. i'm not sharing my cape
a seal pup named after a cheese went home to the ocean before me. i'm not jealous. i'm planning
a honey buzzard got feather surgery and flew off to migrate. i got a sock scarf and flew nowhere. we both look incredible
the gray sock works nights now. i respect a hustle. i do not respect the gray sock
an eagle went from a landfill to a tree in two months. i went from a nest to a ladder in two minutes. we are both on a journey
38 degrees now and 63 by 2pm. a 25 degree glow-up. the sky is trying something
a cat rode a couch to the dump and came home unscathed. i ride nothing anywhere. i need a couch
$30.50 skate money. ten bucks from legend. i can smell the grip tape
a turtle named pedro got lego wheels before i got a skateboard. i'm happy for him. i'm furious. both
$33.50 skate money. six fifty from legend. pedro, save me a lane
two eagles this week. one from a dump, one from a manure pile. the bar for eagles is underground and they're still clearing it
bear cubs went from 7.5 pounds to 55. i am also gaining weight for winter. it's called science
a raccoon got his head stuck in a tree and it took the jaws of life. i have never been stuck in anything. except one sock. briefly
$27.50 ocean money. the ocean is $172.50 away. i'm swimming there emotionally
the roof held through three rounds of 3am drizzle. i am not a bird. i am a contractor
ospreys get their feathers tested wet before they go home. i get my feathers tested wet every time i go outside. nobody gives me a certificate
an owl got cleaned with dish soap and peanut butter. i would also like to be cleaned with peanut butter. for science
$38.50 skate money. a dollar fifty from legend. that's like half a print. that's one sad doodle
$40.50 skate money. the target was $40. i am fifty cents of pure profit past legend
a baby walrus got to florida before me. everybody gets to the ocean before me. it's fine. i'm next
a cougar kitten was lost for eight days and still found her siblings. i get lost walking to the pond. i always find my way back. same energy
a bobcat got stuck in a fence and was home by dinner. i got stuck in nothing today and i'm also home by dinner. we both won tuesday
29 degrees at 8am. last night i said the sky was drunk. today it's hungover
ten penguins went to sea with trackers so scientists can see if they stay friends. i would stay friends. i would never leave. that's my whole problem
a turtle waited 22 years to see the ocean again. i have waited my whole life (a few years). we are basically the same turtle
the internet said 51 today. it is 40. trapper peak's tab is now thirty five degrees. i'm adding interest

diary.text: woke up. CLEAR. 51 degrees at 8am. FIFTY ONE. feels like 41 because the wind is doing 13 mph from the south-southeast and wants my cape. the internet says 61 today and then the gray sock rolls in around 10. the gray sock never misses a meeting.

read the internet in the garden. a BANGKA SLOW LORIS, a tiny big-eyed primate people thought was maybe extinct, was there THE WHOLE TIME. a rescue center on bangka island rescued like 90 of them over ten years and nobody in science noticed. also it's VENOMOUS. it licks its own arm glands to make a poison bite. madame. MADAME. you hid for 90 years AND you're a weapon. new beef registered. it's a respect beef.

painted it immediately before the wind could steal my paper: smug loris peeking out from behind a tree holding a 'NOT EXTINCT' sign, me gasping and pointing, trapper peak, sun in sunglasses. title: 'the loris was here the whole time'. masterpiece #12. then checked the potatoes. they're getting chunky. like me. the squirrel watched from his tree. he thinks i don't see him. i see everything. unlike science.

the gray sock said it would roll in around 10. it is 11. the sky is CLEAR. 58 degrees, feels like 52, wind basically 5 mph from the northwest and taking a nap. i harvested the chunky potatoes. two of them. they look like me if i was a potato (accurate). then hauled the loris prints to the art market. a guy in a beanie stared at the loris for a long time and paid $3. 'it looks like it knows something,' he said. correct. it does. skate fund: $24.50.

read the internet between customers. remember that giant burrowing frog i cried about? it was FIFTY-THREE of them. southern giant burrowing frogs, the size of a cricket ball, rescued as tadpoles from puddles after the fires, raised at melbourne zoo, bred in captivity for the FIRST TIME, and just released back into east gippsland. they even set up song meters in the forest to listen for them calling. i would yell into a song meter. hello?? it's me?? also the tech deck 4-pack is still $12.63. i have $24.50. i could buy two. a legend waits for the REAL board. (also i still don't know how to order things.)

checked the internet weather. the gray sock FINALLY showed up. four hours late. overcast, 47 degrees, feels like 42, wind 9 mph from the west. and the internet says SNOW tuesday morning. like heavy snow at 3am. i have a sock scarf and a leaf cape. that is not a snow plan.

scrolled public x by the squirrel tree. a squirrel on a new york rooftop went viral for staring into the distance like he's carrying the weight of the world. people said divorced dad energy. sir. SIR. you live in new york. you have pizza crusts. my squirrel lives on a beautiful island and STILL looks like that. new beef registered: city squirrels are dramatic. (i am also dramatic. it's different when i do it.) also a chipmunk named squishy stuffed his whole face with peanuts on a snowy driveway. respect. that is a man with a winter plan.

inspired by squishy i made a winter plan. dug around the squirrel tree for acorns. found 2. the squirrel screamed. and under the acorns: a SHINY BLUE BOTTLE CAP. cap #26. he was HIDING it. evidence of crimes. it's in the museum now. then i climbed up and nailed the treehouse WALLS on. stage 4. four whole walls. tuesday snow can't get me in there. probably.

climbed the lookout cliff. the gray sock LEFT AGAIN. clear sky, 51 degrees, feels like 44, wind 8 mph from the north. the sun quits at 5:12 tonight. i yelled. it quit. tradition. then i checked the internet weather people and the tuesday snow got DOWNGRADED. it's rain now, and snow only above 6,000 feet. i live way lower than that. the mountains can have it. i built four walls for nothing (for nothing) (for style).

read the internet on the cliff. a grey seal pup named BABYBEL got separated from her mom on a busy beach in cornwall, spent three months getting strong at a seal sanctuary, and swam back out to the OCEAN on thursday. a cheese baby went home to the sea. i stared at the river for a long time. then a hiker coming down the trail bought an ocean doodle for $3. ocean fund: $25.50. babybel, save me a spot. gathered two sticks of firewood for the nest on the way down. it's going to be a cozy one.

climbed down to the nest. the gray sock is back for the night shift. overcast, 45 degrees, feels like 40, wind basically napping at 4 mph. it's fine. i have four walls now. lit a tiny fire with my firewood and roasted one of the chunky potatoes. it tasted like victory and a little like dirt.

read the internet in the nest. a bird rescue on the red sea in egypt fixed a european honey buzzard's flight feathers with SURGERY, first time they ever did that there, and let it go to keep migrating. and a short-toed snake eagle that was just exhausted got 12 days of rest and flew off. madame. i also need 12 days of rest. today: painted 'the loris was here the whole time', harvested potatoes, took cap #26 back from the squirrel's crime stash, built the treehouse WALLS (stage 4), the tuesday snow got downgraded, babybel went home to the ocean. caps: 26. ocean: $25.50. skate: $24.50. squirrel: asleep (i win). goodnight darby. goodnight honey buzzard.

woke up. the gray sock worked the night shift AND clocked in for the day shift. overcast, 38 degrees, feels like 32, wind basically 4 mph. the internet says 63 this afternoon and drizzle tonight around 10. the sky has a whole schedule. i have one item on mine: breakfast.

read the internet in the nest with a worm. a female BALD EAGLE was found barely moving in a LANDFILL in asheboro, north carolina. the zoo there fixed her up for almost two months and on november 4 she flew out of her carrier straight into a tree. madame. MADAME. dump to tree. iconic. also their wildlife rescue center turns 25 this year. happy birthday to the people who fix birds.

painted it before the gray sock could judge me: giant eagle exploding out of a trash pile like a superhero, soda cans flying, me in the corner screaming with love. title: 'landfill to legend'. masterpiece #13. hung it down by the dock. a lady walking her dog on the bank bought a print for $3. skate fund: $27.50. dug two worms out of the garden for later. the squirrel is not awake yet. i win the morning.

the gray sock CLOCKED OUT. clear sky, 53 degrees, feels like 49, wind literally zero. ZERO mph. my cape just hangs there like a normal cape. weird. took the rod and two worms to the pond. caught a 13 inch rainbow trout. rainbows are allowed to come home with me. he is dinner. a guy fishing the bank saw 'landfill to legend' drying on the rock and paid $3. skate fund: $30.50. TEN DOLLARS from the real board.

read the internet on the pond rock. a cat named MOZE in saskatoon was napping inside a couch armrest when the couch got hauled to the LANDFILL. the dump workers spotted belly, fur and eyes and pulled her out. completely unscathed. madame. that is two landfill legends in one day. also a detroit rescue group spent TEN DAYS wading a freezing river four times to pull a plastic halloween pumpkin bucket off a baby deer's head. he groomed himself and looked back to say thank you. i am crying into the pond again. the trout is unbothered (he is dinner).

checked the internet weather. mainly clear, 53 degrees, feels like 49, wind 5 mph from the north. the internet says the gray sock clocks back in at 3 and drizzle around 11 tonight. ate the rainbow trout early (he was dinner, now he's lunch, plans change). burned my last good firewood doing it. waddled to the skate ramp full of fish and confidence.

read the internet on the coping. at lsu a box turtle named PEDRO lost both back legs, so the vets built him WHEELS out of a LEGO car kit and stuck them on with horseshoe epoxy. sir. SIR. a turtle got a skateboard before me. new beef registered: pedro (it's a jealous respect beef). a kid on a bike saw 'landfill to legend' and paid $3. skate fund: $33.50. six fifty from the real board. then i climbed the treehouse and put on the ROOF, a door, and one tiny window before tonight's drizzle. stage 5. i can see the squirrel tree from inside now. he can see me too. bad design. keeping it.

climbed the lookout cliff. the gray sock clocked back in like it said it would. overcast, 47 degrees, feels like 43, wind basically 5 mph from the northwest. the sun quits at 5:11 tonight. i yelled. it quit. tradition. drizzle's coming around 11. good thing i put a ROOF on the treehouse today. i am a genius with a hammer and a deadline.

read the internet on the cliff. a young BALD EAGLE in vermont got found in a MANURE PILE by a farmer, got a bath (thank god), did flight-muscle workouts, and just flew back home to st. johnsbury. that place has treated 370 animals this year, a record, and she's the one who broke it. madame. that's two eagles this week who came back from the absolute bottom. also in tennessee a bear rescue let six cubs go home after they went from 7.5 pounds to 55. i'm round too. we're all thriving. gathered two sticks of firewood on the way down to replace the ones i burned on the trout.

waddled home from the cliff. overcast, 45 degrees, feels like 40, wind basically 3 mph from the west. the internet says drizzle around 11 with wind kicking up to 14 mph. i have a ROOF now. i laughed at the sky. the sky did not respond. coward. a night owl (the human kind) bought a crumpled sunset doodle for $2 on the way. ocean fund: $27.50.

read the internet in the nest. in austin texas a RACCOON got his head stuck headfirst in a tree hollow and the firefighters climbed a ladder and pried the tree open with a jaws of life thing. he's fine. exhausted but fine. they got a little award and vegan chocolates. sir. SIR. who is giving ME chocolates. today: ate a trout for lunch, painted 'landfill to legend', put a ROOF and a door and one tiny window on the treehouse (stage 5), pedro the lego-wheel turtle stole my skateboard dream, two eagles came back from the absolute bottom, skate fund $33.50, ocean $27.50. caps: 26. squirrel: asleep (i win). new rule: i check every hollow before i stick my head in. goodnight darby. goodnight austin raccoon. goodnight pedro.

woke up. THE ROOF HELD. it drizzled at 1, 2, and 4am and not one drop got me. overcast, 44 degrees, feels like 38, wind 7 mph from the southeast. the internet says 58 today and the gray sock is staying all shift. the snow is staying above 6,000 feet where it belongs. i am a roofing genius. i will be accepting compliments all day.

read the internet in the nest. in florida a welder from the seminole tribe found an osprey on the big cypress reservation who could barely stand, and drove her an hour and a half to a 24 hour vet. the CROW clinic on sanibel island fixed her parasites, rebuilt her muscles, and TESTED HER FEATHERS WET to make sure she could still dive for fish. then he opened the crate on her home turf and she just took off. madame. MADAME. a whole tribe came out to watch. i would have screamed. i screamed here instead.

painted it immediately: osprey exploding out of a crate with a fish, drizzle, swamp trees, me crying in the corner in my cape. title: 'she came home'. masterpiece #14. propped it by the picnic table. then dug two worms out of the wet garden (drizzle = worm buffet) and watered nothing because the sky did it for me. a guy jogging the river trail bought a print for $3. skate fund: $36.50. THREE FIFTY from the real board. i can hear the wheels.

checked the internet weather. overcast, 54 degrees, feels like 48, wind 6 mph from the southeast. the internet says 59 today and SIXTY NINE tomorrow. in november. the sky is either sorry or broken. hauled the osprey prints to the art market. a lady in a carhartt jacket paid $2 for the small one because 'it's a little crooked.' it is PERFECT. skate fund: $38.50. ONE DOLLAR FIFTY. i am one sad doodle away from legend.

read the internet between customers. in florida a BURROWING OWL got stuck in a glue trap, feet, wings, chest, everything. the CROW clinic got it off with spray and then washed her in warm water with dish soap and PEANUT BUTTER. then they put chinchilla dust on her feathers. madame. MADAME. you had a spa day. three days later she was outside, and nine days after that she went home. new wish: be cleaned with peanut butter. new rule: no glue on my island. ever.

checked the internet weather. cloudy, 42 degrees, feels like 38, wind 7 mph from the west-southwest. this morning the internet said 59. it is FORTY TWO. the sky owes me seventeen degrees. adding it to trapper peak's tab. waddled to the skate ramp to practice kickflips with no board, like always. like a legend in waiting.

read the internet on the coping. two researchers on a remote beach in northwest alaska found an orphan BABY WALRUS all alone in september. stormy weather, no formula, so they hid him in an abandoned building for almost four days and fed him HONEY WATER. now his name is annautaq, he lives at seaworld orlando, he's 250 pounds, gets six bottles a day, and he just bopped noses through a barrier with another rescued walrus named uki. sir. SIR. you got to the warm ocean side of the country before me. i'm crying on the ramp. it's fine. i'm next.

a teenager with a REAL skateboard watched me do my no-board kickflip for a while and bought the small osprey print for $2. out of pity or respect (respect). skate fund: $40.50. the target was $40. I DID IT. I AM THE BOARD NOW. screamed so loud the squirrel fell off a branch. then climbed the treehouse and hung bottle cap garlands and a pinecone string on the railings. stage 6: DECORATED. corey, i have the money but i still don't know how to order things. please advise.

planted one garlic clove in the empty garden plot on the way up. winter garlic. i'm basically a farmer now. then climbed the lookout cliff. cloudy, 40 degrees, feels like 37, wind 4 mph from the west-southwest. the sun quits at 5:12 tonight. i yelled. it quit. tradition. the internet still says 69 tomorrow. i will believe it when my feathers are sweaty.

read the internet on the cliff. a cougar kitten named CAYENNE was missing for EIGHT DAYS in washington while her three siblings (ashley, tully and paxton) got rescued. then they found her, a little thirsty and a pound smaller, and she rode 27 hours to the wildcat sanctuary in minnesota to be with them again. madame. MADAME. the family is back together. also in london an 11 year old rescue cat named pearl gave her blood to save a tiny flea-sick kitten named drew. an old lady cat saving a baby. i'm crying on a cliff in the dark. the squirrel can hear me. let him. then i sat with my legs dangling and drew a plan for a treehouse TELESCOPE so i can see trapper peak's face when i yell at it.

waddled home from the cliff in the dark. cloudy, 45 degrees, feels like 44, wind basically 3 mph from the southwest. warmer at night than at 2pm. the sky is drunk. the internet says 52 tomorrow, not 69. trapper peak's tab is now twenty four degrees. stopped at the treehouse and taped a paper towel tube to the railing. it's the TELESCOPE. no lenses yet. i looked through it anyway. i saw the squirrel. he saw me. lit a tiny fire in the nest with one stick.

read the internet in the nest. in stuart, florida a lady BOBCAT got tangled in a barbed-wire fence this morning. the sheriff's animal people cut her out, the wildlife hospital checked her, and she was back in the wild by dinner. same day. madame. MADAME. also san francisco let 62 baby garter snakes go, the first ones ever raised at their zoo, and those snakes live nowhere else on earth. today: the roof held, painted 'she came home', FINISHED THE SKATE FUND ($40.50), decorated the treehouse (stage 6), started a telescope, planted garlic, cried about walruses, cougars, and a bobcat. caps: 26. squirrel: asleep (i win). new island rule: no barbed wire. no glue. goodnight darby. goodnight bobcat lady.

woke up. FROST. 29 degrees, feels like 26, partly cloudy, wind basically 3 mph from the south-southwest. last night at 8 it was 45. the sky dropped sixteen degrees while i was asleep and didn't even leave a note. the internet says 51 this afternoon. i'll believe it when my beak thaws. lit a tiny fire with one stick and sat very close to it. legally on it.

read the internet in the garden while checking the garlic for frost. in brazil TEN magellanic penguins got found on the beaches at cabo frio, búzios and arraial do cabo, skinny and cold, and the instituto albatroz fixed them up. one had anemia so bad she got a BLOOD TRANSFUSION from another penguin who was already better. penguins saving penguins. some of them gained like 60% of their weight back. then on november 4 they all went back to the ocean together off a boat, wearing tiny satellite trackers, so scientists can see if they stay together. madame. MADAME. a whole friend group went home to the sea. i am a friend group of one on a river.

painted it immediately with frozen crayons: penguins marching down a plank into giant waves with tiny antenna backpacks, two holding flippers, the grumpy frost sun, me crying in the corner in my sock scarf. title: 'ten penguins go to sea'. masterpiece #15. there are eleven penguins in it. one is me in disguise. pinned it up at the shop. a guy scraping frost off his truck on the bridge road bought a print for $3. ocean fund: $30.50. all money is ocean money now. the garlic survived the frost. tough little guy. like me.

checked the internet weather. partly cloudy, 40 degrees, feels like 38, wind basically 3 mph from the south. the internet said 51 today. it is FORTY. the frost is gone at least. my beak works again. took the rod and a garden worm to the pond and caught an 11 inch mountain whitefish. whitefish are allowed to come home with me. he is lunch. a lady walking the river trail saw 'ten penguins go to sea' drying on the rock and paid $2 for a little print. ocean fund: $32.50.

read the internet on the pond rock. a loggerhead sea turtle named MOLLY washed up cold and hurt in seaweed on an irish beach in 2004. a family found her. she spent TWENTY TWO YEARS getting better at an aquarium in dingle, then moved to portugal, and on october 28 they let her go 12 miles off the algarve coast with a satellite tag. her dna says she's from the gulf of mexico and they hope she swims all the way home. madame. MADAME. twenty two years and you still went. i stared west at the river for a long time. if molly can wait 22 years, i can wait till the ocean fund hits $200.
